by: the verifier's evidence gate, which maps every claim to implementation evidence
its calibration and self-tests, which check the verifier before its results are trusted
check.population: every claim under investigation and the files that could support it
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the code or document behind a claim changes
check.refusal: a claim with no mapped evidence is reported unverified, and the investigation writes no fix
check.observation: the environment capability probes, which measure the runtime before the workflow relies on it
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the implementation evidence, which a claim is verified against

records.title: Phase-Separated Execution

exemplar.before: An investigation starts fixing gaps and a fix expands its scope, with neither reported.
exemplar.after: detect phase{INVESTIGATE | ACTION} → bind allowed ops → INVESTIGATE{discover, test, document, no-modify} | ACTION{fix known gap, version, no-discovery}

records.intent: Detect the current workflow phase, bind allowed operations to that phase, reject operations outside the phase contract, and emit only the artifact valid for that phase.
records.invariant: A system must separate discovery from mutation so that analysis cannot accidentally remediate and remediation cannot silently expand scope.

records.title: Evidence-Gated Claim Verification

exemplar.before: 'The core has no infra imports' trusted because it sounds right.
exemplar.after: claims → map each to an observable evidence requirement → collect implementation evidence → verdict{verified | contradicted | unverified}

records.intent: Extract claims, resolve each claim into observable evidence requirements, collect direct implementation evidence, classify each claim as verified, contradicted, or unverified, and report discrepancies.
records.invariant: No architectural claim is trusted until mapped to implementation evidence.

records.title: Validation Gate

exemplar.before: A stage's uncertainty stays hidden and flows silently downstream.
exemplar.after: stage → criteria{critical | noncritical} → {PASS | WARN | BLOCK} → block downstream on a critical failure

records.intent: After each critical stage, evaluate declared success criteria, block downstream progression when critical criteria fail, and carry warning-state forward when noncritical criteria fail.
records.invariant: Complex workflows require explicit checkpoints that convert hidden uncertainty into visible control flow.

records.title: File Modification Recovery

exemplar.before: A stale-write failure re-patches the old content, corrupting state.
exemplar.after: edit fail → re-read current → merge the delta into full state → write complete version → verify{exists & content matches}

records.intent: When a file mutation fails because state changed between read and edit, reread the current file, merge the intended delta into the current content, write the complete new version, and verify persistence.
records.invariant: Treat stale-write failures as state synchronization failures, not as patch failures.

records.title: Trust Anchor Declaration

exemplar.before: The verifier's own axioms are hidden, so its boundary is unknowable.
exemplar.after: declare minimal assumptions{runtime, filesystem, execution, tool IO} → boundary{cannot verify the verifier} → disclosed, not verified

records.intent: Declare the minimum assumptions required for the system to verify anything, bind all verification logic to those assumptions, and disclose the verification boundary.
records.invariant: Every axiom a verifier rests on is declared explicitly.

records.title: Environment Capability Verification

exemplar.before: Advanced analysis relied on before checking the runtime can run it.
exemplar.after: requirements{runtime, package manager, write, filesystem} → probe each → classify by severity → mode{full | degraded | blocked}

records.intent: Before executing advanced behavior, probe required runtime dependencies, classify each dependency failure by severity, and degrade or block capability based on criticality.
records.invariant: Runtime capability must be measured before the workflow relies on it.

records.title: Tool Calibration

exemplar.before: A detector's match trusted with no control test.
exemplar.after: known-good + known-bad fixtures → run tool → detect false-positive AND false-negative → reliable only if both controls pass

records.intent: Create known-good and known-bad fixtures, run the verification tool against both, detect false positives and false negatives, and mark the tool reliable only if both controls pass.
records.invariant: Verification tools must be tested against controls before their results are trusted.

records.title: Behavioral Self-Test

exemplar.before: A claimed capability trusted without ever running it on a case.
exemplar.after: claimed behavior → positive + negative case → execute → compare → {matches contract | false-positive | false-negative | failed}

records.intent: Execute the system’s claimed behaviors against simple positive and negative cases, compare actual output to expected output, and treat mismatch as implementation evidence failure.
records.invariant: A capability counts only once its behavior matches a testable contract.

records.title: Adversarial Input Testing

exemplar.before: A detector accepted after ordinary examples pass, never tested hostilely.
exemplar.after: attacks{pathTraversal, nullByte, unicodeHomoglyph, commentFalsePositive, patternSpoof} → run detector → {blocked | ignored | vulnerable}

records.intent: Generate malicious, malformed, ambiguous, and deceptive inputs, execute the detection logic against them, and classify whether the system resists or accepts invalid patterns.
records.invariant: Verification logic must be tested against hostile inputs, not only ordinary examples.

records.title: Defensive String Normalization

exemplar.before: A raw external string passed straight to a filesystem or command boundary.
exemplar.after: raw string → null-guard → strip{'../', null byte} → Unicode NFC → only the sanitized string crosses a boundary

records.intent: Reject null input, remove dangerous path/control patterns, normalize Unicode representation, and only pass sanitized strings to filesystem, parser, or command boundaries.
records.invariant: All external strings must be converted from hostile representation into bounded representation before use.

records.title: Safe Arithmetic Contract

exemplar.before: A division runs unchecked and returns NaN or Infinity into a decision.
exemplar.after: operands → preconditions{denominator != 0, finite} → compute → postconditions{isFinite, within bounds} → number | null | typed failure

records.intent: Check operands before calculation, reject division by zero, reject non-finite results, enforce bounds, and return nullable or typed failure instead of unsafe numeric state.
records.invariant: Arithmetic output is only valid if the operation and result both satisfy the numeric contract.

records.title: Recursion Control

exemplar.before: A recursive self-reference runs away with no depth bound.
exemplar.after: enter → increment depth → depth <= max? → {continue | reject max-depth} → unwind on exit

records.intent: Increment depth on recursive entry, compare against maximum depth, reject excessive recursion, and unwind depth on completion.
records.invariant: Recursive systems require explicit depth governance to prevent runaway self-reference.

records.title: Recursive Self-Verification

exemplar.before: The verifier exempts itself from its own rules and overclaims.
exemplar.after: self definition → extract self-claims → search implementation evidence → discrepancies → confidence{confirmed | overclaimed | invalid}

records.intent: Load the system’s own definition, extract self-claims, search for implementation evidence of each claim, classify discrepancies, and downgrade confidence when self-description exceeds implemented behavior.
records.invariant: A verifier should apply its verification rules to itself.

records.title: Advanced Tool Escalation

exemplar.before: A capability gap filled by inference instead of evidence.
exemplar.after: analysis need → capability gap → write script → execute → parse → integrate the result as evidence

records.intent: When direct tools cannot answer a verification question, synthesize a specialized analyzer, execute it against the target, parse its output, and integrate the result as evidence.
records.invariant: Missing capability should trigger controlled tool construction rather than unsupported inference.

records.title: Investigation Report

exemplar.before: An investigation that also 'quickly fixes' what it found.
exemplar.after: evidence → findings + risks + adversarial results + confidence → one investigation report, no remediation

records.intent: Collect verified findings, failed checks, warnings, discrepancies, environmental limits, adversarial results, and confidence level into a structured report without performing remediation.

records.title: Action Log

exemplar.before: A fix run against a gap that was never documented, discovering new scope mid-flight.
exemplar.after: documented gaps only → bounded fix → version → verify write → action log; discovers nothing new

records.intent: Accept only documented gaps as input, apply bounded changes, version the modified artifact, verify the write, and emit an action log without discovering new scope.
records.invariant: Remediation operates only on known evidence.

records.title: Contract-Based Verification Kernel

exemplar.before: Behavior trusted because it looks right, with no phase, calibration, or self-check.
exemplar.after: declare assumptions → detect phase → verify environment → calibrate tools → phase-legal execution → adversarial test → validation gate → self-verify → typed artifact

records.intent: Declare assumptions, detect phase, verify environment, calibrate tools, execute phase-legal behavior, test adversarially, enforce validation gates, self-verify claims, and emit a typed artifact.
records.invariant: A reusable verification kernel is a gated state machine whose transitions are evidence-bound and phase-constrained.

records.title: <Context Verification Concern>
records.intent: <Detect required contract> → <Bind allowed capability> → <Execute bounded operation> → <Validate evidence> → <Emit typed result>
records.invariant: <Any system behavior should be treated as a contract-bound transition whose legitimacy depends on phase, evidence, and postcondition verification.>
